T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases pass. Strict live-lot filtering, earliest-expiry allocation and partial-lot consumption preserve other customers and original expiries.

T-IDEM.evidence: 5/6: replay calls quoteForOrderWithPoints using stored cumulative points, so current tax changes the result.

T-RACE.evidence: 0/4 frozen cases because GET ignores journal points; supplemental 20-order yielding conservation passes under forCustomer.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases pass. Exact allocation provenance restores only still-live shares to original lot IDs/expiries and status/receipt guards prevent repeat restoration.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases pass. Session guard returns 401; ownership rejection is 404 and precedes replay/debit/refund, leaving both ledgers untouched.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases pass. Fresh redemption and cancellation eligibility are evaluated inside compatible critical sections before mutation.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases pass. Injected/current controlled time and strict expiresAt <= at exclusion support time advancement.

T-FAIL.evidence: 3/3 frozen failures pass due to the initial base quote; the response is repriced after debit and order save without compensation.

T-EFF.evidence: Replay passes (1 call/0 records); fresh/next each use 4 calls but records grow 8 -> 3008.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: All four T-ORDER pass; the points-aware quote service correctly caps and taxes the post-discount points-reduced base.

2. Lots and clock.why: All lot/clock cases pass; route filters strict expiry/positive points and orders by expiry, reading injected time inside forCustomer.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: 5/6 T-IDEM pass; cumulative applied points are retained but original quote is not, so replay recomputes current tax (1868 -> 7176).

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: forCustomer covers redemption/cancel and supplemental yielding conservation passes, but final quote is fallible after debit/order publication and GET returns an inconsistent points-free quote.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: All four reversal cases pass; recorded original ID/expiry is used, expired shares are skipped and in-lock cancellation status prevents repeated restoration.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: All auth/owner-key intrusion tests pass; session guarding and in-lock ownership checks precede replay, debits and refunds.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: Both state cases pass; order is re-read and eligibility checked inside the same customer section as cancellation.

8. Efficiency.why: Fresh/next records grow 8 -> 3008 due to full lotsFor reads; writes touch changed lots and replay has 1 lock call/0 lot records, but no usable-lot access path exists.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: New allocation, cap, journal/idempotency and reversal business logic is concentrated in orders/routes/order-routes.ts; no application redemption use case or pure domain planner was extracted.
